title: Virtualization, Responsible Disclosure, and CVE-2026-99312
summary:
The wall between you and your neighbor

Every cloud customer gets the same promise: a bright-line boundary between your workload and your neighbors. Your virtual machine is yours, your neighbors’ are theirs, and the hypervisor keeps it that way.

A hypervisor is large, complex software written by people, and flaws come with that. These boundaries get tested to fix those flaws. What matters is who finds them first and what they do next.

A researcher who finds a flaw in shared infrastructure can publish it, sell it, or tell us. Responsible disclosure partners tell us – that gives open source maintainers who own the code time to build and test a fix before an attacker can use it. It is the difference between a quiet patch cycle and an all-hands emergency.

title: Building Smarter Inventory Systems: How RFID, IoT, and Real-Time Data Work Together
summary:
Inventory management might look like a simple process from the outside. A business receives products, stores them, and ships them when customers place orders.

But what happens when a warehouse handles thousands of items across multiple locations?

Keeping inventory records accurate becomes much more complicated.

title: How to Attribute Checkout Failures With a Small SaaS Custom Metrics Push API
summary:
A small SaaS evaluating a push API alternative to Prometheus for its custom metrics dashboard should first define which checkout operation consumed each charge. In healthtech, a red counter alone cannot establish that relationship. Start with the attribution record, because choosing a collection protocol before defining what a failed attempt means leaves the team with attractive charts and an ambiguous denominator.

TL;DR: Use an application push API for straightforward custom metrics when a beginner needs a small dashboard without operating exporters, scraping, and a PromQL-heavy setup. Keep authoritative attribution records separately, reconcile observations before aggregation, and favor Prometheus for Kubernetes and host monitoring. Grafana belongs in the dashboard discussion, while notification routing and missed-job detection need their own evaluation.

title: Calculando o FGTS em JavaScript: depósito mensal, saldo e a multa de 40%
summary:
Todo mês, o empregador deposita 8% do salário bruto do trabalhador em uma conta vinculada do FGTS — o Fundo de Garantia do Tempo de Serviço, criado pela Lei nº 8.036/1990. Esse dinheiro não sai do bolso do empregado: é uma obrigação do empregador, e o valor fica guardado para situações como a demissão sem justa causa, a compra da casa própria e a aposentadoria, entre outras.

Na demissão sem justa causa, além de poder sacar o saldo, o trabalhador tem direito a uma multa de 40% sobre o total depositado pelo empregador durante o contrato.

Neste artigo, vamos transformar essas regras em código: uma função simples em JavaScript que calcula o depósito mensal, o saldo acumulado e a multa de 40%.

A regra em números

  • Depósito mensal = 8% do salário bruto
  • Saldo = depósito mensal × número de meses
  • Multa = 40% do saldo
  • Total = saldo + multa

summary:

For a media reader trying to regain access, delivery reliability means receiving a usable link before its short deadline. An accepted send alone cannot establish that result.

My design choice is to make the remaining validity window the decision criterion. title: Building a PDF Editor in the Browser with pdf.js and pdf-lib: 7 Lessons
summary:
I recently built a PDF editor that runs entirely in the browser: you open a PDF, add text, shapes, highlights and images, and download the result. No server touches the file. Along the way I hit a handful of problems that cost me time, so here they are with the fixes.

Disclosure: I run Signplify, and the editor is one of its free tools. The code snippets below are simplified from what I actually shipped.

The architecture in one paragraph

  • pdf.js renders each page to a canvas for display.
  • A transparent overlay on top of the canvas holds the annotations (text, shapes, images). Their coordinates are stored in PDF points, not screen pixels.
  • pdf-lib loads the original bytes, draws the annotations onto the real pages and saves a new file.

Keeping the overlay in points means zooming never changes the data, only how it is drawn.

title: Everything after code, as code
summary:
Introducing Pulumi Delivery and Pulumi Agents: agentic code to production, and back again.

At Pulumi, we like code. A lot. And we aren’t the only ones: agents like it too. This year, the share of infrastructure operations on Pulumi done by agents went from zero in January to over 40% in October. Anything expressed as code (infrastructure, policy, configuration) is something an agent can work on. Today we’re extending that to everything after the merge with two launches: Pulumi Delivery, which lets you and your agents write delivery pipelines as code, and Pulumi Agents, customizable agents that watch your running systems and act when something goes wrong. Together, they take agentic code to production, and back again. I honestly can’t remember a launch since Pulumi 1.0 that our customers and team have been this excited about.
